points.point: **Le gros cycle du runtime moteur existe toujours** : j’en détecte encore un sur **49 fichiers** dans `game/engine/runtime`, autour de `game-definition-*`, `game-context-*`, `effects-*`, `patterns/*`, `recipes/*`, `movement-kit`, `pawn-kit`, `phase-kit`, lifecycle et configuration. C’est actuellement le principal point empêchant de considérer l’architecture moteur comme complètement découplée.
points.analysis: Removed the runtime strongly connected component. All 152 production files form an acyclic graph including type imports, re-exports, dynamic imports and TypeScript aliases. A regression audit rejects every cycle without a baseline.

points.point: **Le cycle `player-values-kit.ts ↔ numeric-invariants.ts` existe toujours** : les invariants numériques doivent devenir totalement indépendants du kit qui les consomme.
points.analysis: numeric-invariants depends on player-values-contracts, never on its consuming controller.

points.point: **Le cycle TypeORM `RoomEntity ↔ RoomParticipantEntity ↔ RoomBotEntity` existe toujours** : il faut décider si les relations bidirectionnelles sont réellement nécessaires ; sinon privilégier des références par ID et des chargements explicites.
points.analysis: Room child relations use a structural persistence projection and the named ORM target; metadata tests preserve inverse relations and cascading foreign keys.

points.point: **La direction des dépendances internes du moteur n’est toujours pas strictement descendante** : plusieurs couches bas niveau connaissent encore des structures de définition/compilation qui redépendent ensuite d’elles.
points.analysis: Execution entry points no longer depend transitively on the definition compiler, definition validator, pattern builders or recipe builders. Low-level author commands and independently owned contracts establish a descending acyclic dependency graph. The audit also rejects indirect upward paths.

points.point: **Il manque toujours une séparation plus nette `AuthorGameDefinition -> CompiledGameDefinition -> Runtime`** : les structures d’authoring et d’exécution restent encore trop proches.
points.analysis: Author/compiled/runtime contracts still share callback structures; no full separation completed.

points.point: **Il manque toujours une IR compilée neutre** : une représentation intermédiaire indépendante des builders, patterns, recipes et executors permettrait probablement de casser une grande partie du cycle de 49 fichiers.
points.analysis: Neutral effect IR exists, but a complete compiled game IR independent of all builders/executors is still missing.

points.point: **`game-definition-contracts.ts` reste trop central** : il concentre encore de nombreux concepts et participe directement au grand cycle.
points.analysis: Split author rules, pattern fragments, effect resolvers, validation input, configuration state and persistent runtime state out of the compiled definition contract. The remaining definition contract no longer participates in any cycle.

points.point: **Les patterns restent trop liés au runtime/definition compiler** : idéalement ils devraient produire des fragments déclaratifs sans connaître la couche d’exécution.
points.analysis: Pattern fragments now depend on independent author rule/context contracts and kit primitives. They no longer acquire the execution context class or compiler through these contracts. Existing composition behavior is preserved.

points.point: **Les recipes restent trop liées aux structures supérieures du moteur** : elles devraient dépendre uniquement de primitives/contracts suffisamment bas niveau.
points.analysis: Recipes import low-level action builders and author rule contracts directly. Action and choice builders and their typed handler adapter no longer import the compiled definition or definition compiler.

points.point: **Les effects restent fortement interconnectés avec definitions, validators et runtime execution** : définition, validation et exécution doivent être séparées plus strictement.
points.analysis: Effect instruction/resolver contracts, author effect capability, typed builder adapter, validation inputs and execution are separate. Effect execution cannot reach the game compiler/validator/pattern/recipe builders through its imports.

points.point: **Le lifecycle reste pris dans le même graphe cyclique** : `game-turn-controller`, `game-turn-schedule` et hooks devraient dépendre d’un modèle compilé minimal plutôt que de structures qui redépendent du lifecycle.
points.analysis: Turn controller and turn schedule use minimal TurnRuntimeState and TurnScheduleState contracts instead of the full declarative state/compiled definition. Lifecycle hooks use the independently owned author context. Their transitive imports are acyclic.

points.point: **`GameRuleContext` reste au centre du gros cycle** : même s’il a été amélioré, il reste une façade très large du runtime.
points.analysis: The runtime context implements the independently owned GameContextCapabilities interface. Author context no longer derives its contract by importing the runtime class. Compile-time bidirectional compatibility and forbidden orchestration API assertions preserve the existing public surface.

points.point: **Les capacités de `GameRuleContext` devraient encore être davantage segmentées** : lifecycle, players, components, interactions, effects, scheduling et values devraient être des sous-capabilities plus indépendantes.
points.analysis: Segmented player, lifecycle, value, component, interaction, effect and scheduling capabilities into independently owned contracts. Turn/configuration/effect command ports are explicit; other controllers expose structural public views. Existing facade aliases remain compatible.

points.point: **`GameContextFor` peut encore être renforcé** : le type devrait exposer uniquement les capabilities réellement activées par la définition compilée du jeu.
points.analysis: Component filtering is verified, but scheduler and other capability inference are incomplete.

points.point: **Un jeu n’utilisant pas Cards devrait idéalement ne pas avoir `ctx.cards` dans son contexte typé**.
points.analysis: GameContextFor removes Cards for definitions without Cards components; negative type assertions compile and Cards remains available when declared.

points.point: **Même principe pour Movement, Inventory, Economy, Quiz, Voting, Scheduler et les autres kits optionnels**.
points.analysis: Cards/Movement/Inventory/Economy/Quiz/Voting filters are tested; Scheduler remains exposed.

points.point: **Les références JSON entre composants doivent être validées avant runtime** : deck IDs, track IDs, resource IDs, phase IDs, effects, actions, pawns, etc.
points.analysis: The supported closed JSON grammar rejects unsupported components. JSON compilation now delegates all static reference checks to the common definition validator, removing its divergent reference index. Actions, card content, track landing effects, nested conditions and reaction branches/options are checked against component/resource/action/phase/effect catalogues before runtime. Added regression tests for missing references inside cards and reaction availability, and for numeric/string card identity separation. Extending the JSON language remains tracked by 18/19.
points.continuation: JSON authoring now has an executable closed version-1 profile, but production games, all optional components, patterns and the complete Panier Express rules are not migrated. This broader point remains open.

points.point: **Les incompatibilités de capability doivent être détectées à compilation** : par exemple un effet Cards dans un jeu qui n’a pas de composant Cards.
points.analysis: Static declarative effects and conditions cannot compile without their required hand/deck/track/dice/inventory/resource catalogues. Reaction availability now validates each option against the hand card catalogue or declared resources. The common validator owns this rule for both authoring paths. Unsupported JSON components are rejected by the closed grammar; dynamic TypeScript callback capability inference remains separately tracked by 14/16.
points.continuation: JSON authoring now has an executable closed version-1 profile, but production games, all optional components, patterns and the complete Panier Express rules are not migrated. This broader point remains open.

points.point: **Le langage JSON auteur doit rester fermé et typé** : pas d’expression JavaScript ou pseudo-code dans des strings.
points.analysis: The author JSON boundary accepts only bounded plain JSON data and an explicit closed grammar. No strings are interpreted as code; custom effects without engine resolvers are rejected.

points.point: **Le schema auteur JSON doit être versionné**.
points.analysis: Author documents require schemaVersion 1. Missing or unsupported versions are rejected before compilation.

points.point: **La version du contenu doit rester distincte de la version du runtime**.
points.analysis: Author schema, content label/fingerprint, game-state schema and engine algorithm version are distinct. Changing JSON with unchanged labels changes the effective content fingerprint.

points.point: **La version de définition du jeu doit être explicitement distinguée des autres versions si nécessaire**.
points.analysis: JSON definitionVersion explicitly feeds compiled rulesVersion, separately from the author schema, content fingerprint and engine algorithm.

points.point: **Les snapshots doivent embarquer suffisamment d’information de version pour garantir leur restauration future**.
points.analysis: Snapshot headers are verified, but migration/restore guarantees for future incompatible runtimes remain incomplete.

points.point: **Les migrations de snapshot doivent être prévues pour les changements runtime incompatibles**.
points.analysis: Engine-owned snapshot migration registry resolves a bounded unambiguous path before transforming a clone. Real multi-step transformations, missing paths, cycles, invalid output and identity preservation are tested. Headerless legacy snapshots remain tied to engine 1, never to an arbitrary future current version. No incompatible engine version is being introduced.

points.point: **Panier Express n’est toujours pas démontré comme jeu 100 % déclaratif**.
points.analysis: Panier Express still contains TypeScript-specific rules and cannot be claimed 100% declarative.
points.continuation: JSON authoring now has an executable closed version-1 profile, but production games, all optional components, patterns and the complete Panier Express rules are not migrated. This broader point remains open.

points.point: **Il manque toujours la preuve qu’un jeu utilisant uniquement des mécaniques connues peut être ajouté sans `.ts` spécifique**.

The actual CLI-generated JSON package was also compiled and played using the production build. The fixture is deliberately outside the production catalogue.

points.point: **Les phases terminales doivent être identifiées explicitement**.
points.analysis: Compilation requires explicit terminal metadata for phases with no exits and rejects outgoing edges from terminal phases. Both TypeScript and JSON authoring tests cover these invariants.

points.point: **Les transitions invalides doivent être impossibles après compilation**.
points.analysis: Compiled phase graphs reject missing/unreachable targets and invalid terminal exits. Recursive freezing now traverses shallow-frozen author phases, so retained transition arrays cannot add edges after compilation. Runtime rejects forbidden transitions before exit hooks, timer cancellation or state mutation; repeated same-phase requests are idempotent. Compilation and transition contract tests pass.

points.point: **Les structures persistées dans les snapshots doivent rester entièrement sérialisables**.
points.analysis: Snapshot validation rejects nonserializable values. State creation deep-clones base/turn/player data and creates independent kit storage; isolation and state-loader tests pass.

points.point: **Le contenu compilé doit rester réellement immutable**.
points.analysis: Compiled static collections now expose immutable read facades backed by isolated private collections. Direct and borrowed Map/Set prototype mutators cannot modify them, iterators and forEach cannot leak the backing collection, and retained source aliases cannot mutate the compiled copy. Recursive freezing handles shallow-frozen and readonly parents and preserves shared identities. The final compiler applies this protection to its entire visible graph, including manually supplied content contracts. Content cloning and card materialization preserve collection entries without exposing mutable catalogues; content fingerprints and snapshot formats are unchanged.

points.point: **Deux parties ne doivent jamais partager des références mutables provenant d’un même contenu initial**.
